The metasurface is based on a metal cut-wire structure with a copper front layer and FR4 dielectric substrate of thickness 3.5 mm.
The basic unit cell period is 10 mm.
Element '1' is a 90° rotation of element '0', producing a 180° cross-polarization reflection phase difference.
Polarization conversion ratio reaches up to 90% across 6–14 GHz and peaks near 99% at resonance.
The metasurface achieves RCS reduction greater than 10 dB on average in the 6–14 GHz range.
Maximum experimental RCS reduction observed is 37 dB at 10.5 GHz.
The metasurface reduces RCS by redirecting scattered energy rather than absorbing it.
The design uses a Fabry-Perot-like resonance cavity formed by the metal layers and dielectric spacer.
Simulations and experiments show good agreement in reflectance and RCS reduction results.
RCS reduction decreases with increasing incidence angle but remains effective up to 30°.
Coding sequences 01/01 and 01/10 provide effective RCS reduction; 01/10 is polarization-insensitive.
The metasurface sample size for experiments was 400 × 400 mm².
The metasurface is fabricated using traditional PCB technology.
The cross-polarization reflection coefficients are greater than 0.85 in the operating band.
Co-polarization reflection coefficients are substantially less than 0.3 at resonance frequencies.
The metasurface operates by controlling scattering direction through phase gradient coding.
The array factor of the metasurface is derived using planar array theory.
The metasurface is designed to reduce detection probability by infrared devices by scattering energy irregularly.
The research was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China and Hubei Province.
The metasurface has potential applications in stealth technology.
